key_insight: As doping and vacancy engineering in MoS2 monolayers tune the electronic structure by introducing midgap defect states and shifting the Fermi level, enabling either p-type or n-type behavior depending on defect site.
engineering_relevance: These defect-driven band modifications suggest a practical route to optimize MoS2 for photocatalysis, photovoltaics, and FET performance through targeted atomic-scale doping.
method: Performed first-principles density functional theory (DFT) calculations on MoS2 monolayers.
Compared pristine material with S vacancies, Mo vacancies, As substituting Mo, As substituting S, and As interstitial configurations.
Analyzed structural changes and electronic properties via defect-state and Fermi-level behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports defect-induced midgap states and distinct Fermi-level shifts: p-type behavior for V_S, V_Mo, As-Mo, and As-S, and n-type behavior for the As interstitial system.
watch_item: The conclusions come from DFT-only modeling, so experimental synthesis stability and real-device performance still need validation.
paper_title: First-principles study of the impact of As doping on the structural and electronic properties of MoS$_2$ monolayer
